summary: Jim Rheingans is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the University of Hamburg and a PhD at the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.
Jim Taylor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University by 1989 and was attested in 2014 as a Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide.

Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and has been a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jinah Kim works in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams, was a Mellon fellow at the Institute for Advanced Study (2009–2010), and held posts at Vanderbilt and Harvard.
Jinavijaya Muni (1888–1976) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Principal at Gujarat Vidyapith and founded Rajasthan Puratana Granthamala (attested 1959).

Jinbo Shi (born 1940) specializes in history, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Minzu University and under Jingru Wang at CASS, he held posts at CASS from 1975, Minzu University, North Minzu University, and Ningxia University.
Jinchuan Wan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held professorships at National Central University and Fo Guang University, both attested in 2010.
Jing Yin specializes in Buddhist studies. A former student of K. L. Dhammajoti, he served as a Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

Jing-shen Tao (born 1933) is a historian and sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University (PhD ~1967), later serving as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000) and Correspondence Research Fellow at Academia Sinica.
Jingru Wang (1903–1990) was a linguistics and history scholar. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1928–1930) and held a post at Minzu University of China (~1952–1958).

Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After graduate studies at McMaster and postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki, he held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of British Columbia.

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned her PhD at the University of Colorado under Paul W. Kroll. She held posts at Harvard, City University of Hong Kong, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
Jinling He specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Koki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Jinshi Fan (born 1938) is a history/archaeology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Su Bai at Peking University (~1958–1963) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) as well as professor at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked at Wuhan University until 1986 and subsequently served at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017) as dean of its archaeological institute and researcher.
Jiro Abe (1883–1959) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907) and held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1922) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology. Educated at Kyoto University (~1938–1941), he held faculty positions at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1969–1979), University of Tsukuba (~1979–1984), and Chubu University (~1984–1990).

Jiro Murata (1895–1985) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1970).

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953) and held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1953–1988), Nagaoka University of Technology, Bukkyo University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
